newsitem.title: USA: Picturetel sees markets continuing weak.
newsitem.headline: Picturetel sees markets continuing weak.

text.p: PictureTel Corp said it expected weakness in its videoconferencing markets to continue through "several quarters" after it posted a loss for the second quarter.

The company, which posted a net loss of $0.09 per share, compared to a profit of $0.24 per share a year ago said that revenues fell and it slipped to an operating loss because of weak demand and lower average selling prices for its products in the U.S. and Europe.
Revenues slid to $112.2 million from a $116.1 million a year ago.

"Despite this weakness in the marketplace, which we expect will continue for several quarters, PictureTel continues to command more than 50 percent of the revenue in the worldwide videoconferencing market," said Norman E. Gaut, PictureTel's chairman and CEO.
He said that in the light of expected poor demand, Picturetel would cut costs and expected to be able to reduce expenses by 10-15 percent.
The company also said that it expected to post a charge of $10-15 million in the third quarter due to reorganisation and costs of the acquisition and integration of MultiLink.
